title: Hiring Lockjaw Davis and teaching young players
summary: He heard Lockjaw jamming at Minton's, took time to teach talent to read, and says he learned from Goodman.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Well, I'll tell you -- oh, it's Lockjaw. I wanted to ask you about Lockjaw. Where did you hear lockjaw?
Lockjaw? Lockjaw was quite young and I think -- where did I hear Lockjaw? It was down at Minton's, I think. I think I heard him down at Minton's, jamming.
This was after you'd had the band a couple of years or so, I guess.
I mean, this was after Charlie Parker, wasn't it?
Yeah. And you liked what you heard?
Yeah. I liked what I heard.
I mean, I don't think he -- he hadn't been playing with a lot of people then, had he? Or had he?
I'm the first big band he played with.
Well, Lockjaw wasn't so schooled on reading. Am I right?
Yeah. He made it all right with me.
Yeah. Because during that period of time, if a guy had a little talent, I would take time for him to learn how to read. And to bring it out of him.

And teaching him. That's a good way. That's a part of -- Benny didn't teach anyone, but he schooled the guys that he hired. They knew how to read, but they didn't know how to phrase or anything, and I could picture myself setting there in front of the band, picture Benny setting there in front of the band, stopping them and telling them what to do. And I did the same thing.
You did. Sing it for them.
And that's the reason I took it. I learned a lot from Goodman, you know.
Yeah. Well, did any of these guys ever tell you thank you, later?
Yeah. A lot of them thanked me.
Well, you had a happy band, I take it.
On the whole, I take it.

Yeah. Well, I was very good in finding talent and bringing it out of them. It was in the rough and raw. But I would work with it very hard. In later years I stopped doing it, because my patience wasn't so good.
Yeah. Time takes its toll, doesn't it?
